facts.claim: There is no consensus on whether germline genome editing has any substantial advantages over existing procedures like embryo selection after in vitro fertilization (IVF) and preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD).
facts.quote: However, when it comes to the most controversial topic, germline genome editing (GGE), there is no consensus on whether this technology has any substantial advantages over existing procedures such as embryo selection after in vitro fertilization (IVF) and preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD).

facts.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 technology is characterized by easy handling, high accuracy, and low cost.
facts.quote: Among them, CRISPR-Cas9 technology particularly stands out due to its advantages such as easy handling, high accuracy, and low cost.

facts.claim: There are some scenarios where only germline intervention allows couples to have biologically related healthy offspring because selection will not avoid disease.
facts.quote: The paper confirms that there are some scenarios in which only germline intervention allows couples to have (biologically related) healthy offspring, because selection will not avoid disease.

facts.claim: He Jiankui used CRISPR to edit embryos, two of which became living babies in October 2018.
facts.quote: He Jiankui had used clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats ('CRISPR') to edit embryos-two of which had, sometime in October, become living babies.

facts.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 can correct disease-causing mutations and restore normal gene function.
facts.quote: CRISPR–Cas9 enables precise gene editing, correcting disease-causing mutations and offering hope for previously incurable genetic conditions.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

research.angle: While CRISPR-Cas9 offers precise gene editing for diseases, there is no consensus that it provides substantial advantages over existing methods like preimplantation genetic diagnosis.
research.verdict: The sources confirm the technical capability of CRISPR for gene editing but do not provide evidence of a wealth-based biological class divide or specific aesthetic enhancements.
research.caveat: None of the provided sources mention wealth, social class, aesthetics, or cognitive traits.
